pages.title: Multi-Region Active-Active Platform on AWS (10M Users)

finalAnswer:
[Multi-region active-active platform on AWS](<temp>\project\.archi-made-easy\architecture-multi-region-aws-20261110-222519\multi-region-aws.html)

Two full-stack regions behind Route 53 latency routing and CloudFront, with DynamoDB global tables as the bidirectional store — so a regional loss is a routing event, not a failover procedure. The hard parts are in the cards: write-conflict resolution, regional Cognito user pools, and each region carrying 100% of load alone.

What I assumed (you gave only "AWS", "multi-region", "10 million users"):
- us-east-1 / eu-west-1 as example regions — pick from your real user geography and residency rules.
- Key-value primary store; relational workloads would need Aurora Global Database (one writer region) instead, noted on the page.
- No peak RPS, latency, availability or budget targets, so no traffic/latency/cost figures are authored anywhere.

Read it as a system overview: S3 with cross-region replication, observability and CI/CD are described in the notes rather than drawn, and WAF/Shield appear as a tag on CloudFront instead of a separate box.

The page's Workbench button (and the Review/Simulate/Optimize rail on the left) lets you try region failures, traffic multipliers and variants yourself. Its built-in review scores this design 94 with one medium finding — the synchronous read path user → DNS → edge → ALB → services → DynamoDB — plus missing RPO/RTO on DynamoDB, which needs your numbers. Those results are an analytical model of the declared design, not measurements.
